name: Can a walk-in shower be built over an old tile floor?

mainEntity.name: Can a new walk-in shower be installed over an existing tile floor, or does the old floor need to be removed first?
mainEntity.text: Can a new walk-in shower be installed over an existing tile floor, or does the old floor need to be removed first?

acceptedAnswer.text: In most cases, a walk-in shower should not simply be built over an old tile floor without a full evaluation of the layers underneath. The existing tile may look solid, but the subfloor, waterproofing, and framing beneath it could be damaged or improperly sloped. To build a durable shower, the contractor usually needs access to the structure so the drain, membrane, and floor pitch can be installed correctly. Reusing an old tile floor can create height issues, weak transitions, and hidden moisture problems. In some rare situations, a contractor may work with part of an existing floor assembly, but that depends on the bathroom structure, the shower footprint, and whether the old materials are sound. For most homeowners, full removal is the safer path because it lets the new shower be built as a proper waterproof system rather than a cosmetic overlay.
acceptedAnswer.description: A walk-in shower usually should not be built directly over an old tile floor unless the existing structure has been evaluated and the new assembly is designed for that condition. Most remodels require removal of old finishes so the contractor can inspect the subfloor, correct slope, and install proper waterproofing. Hidden damage is common under old tile.
